questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very important to me that the courses were good and I knew I had a lot to choose from at the Complutense which is why I chose that university. It was also very important for me that the professors were good, which they were, and I also knew I wanted to live in Madrid as I have a strong connection to that city. It also looks good on my CV that I have been at the UCM, because I know it is one of the best places to study spanish philology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to get information, because if I couldn't find it somewhere I would just write to the Erasmus office at the Complutense who were always ready to help, so I didn't have any noticable problems upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office at the UCM were very good at giving information and answering emails etc. There was also a welcome session at the complutense which was nice because there I got to meet other erasmus students as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult because it was hard for me to know who I could trust online. The UCM recommended me some websites, but it still felt a bit insecure. However, there were a lot of possibilities and I got to live in my favorite area in Madrid, Malasaña, which was very nice. I lived with Smart Living which I found on HousingAnywhere, and I liked the location of the apartment a lot, however the apartment itself was not the best as it didn't have a living room and we had problems with hot water etc. The company were ready to help, but the problems kept coming back, so I am not sure if I would recommend that company.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be quite expensive to live in the centre of Madrid and you also need to think about whether your apartment is located close to a square because that produces a lot of noise. However, it was no problem for me living off campus, because the metro is very quick in Madrid.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit annoying that I could not get into a student housing on campus, I wrote to the erasmus office and asked, but they told me that it is only meant for spanish students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to the erasmus office and they signed my paper.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a meeting for Erasmus students right at the beginnning.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very sucessful, it went very smoothly. I had to change several classes, however, it was very easy to make the changes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the first two weeks of the semester we got to try out all classes we wanted, which I would recommend other students to do before they confirm their final classes, because it's nice to see whether or not you like the teacher etc. before signing up for the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I absolutely loved it, really felt like I learned a lot!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 5 courses and some were harder than others. Especially the literary courses were a bit difficult because the teachers kept making references to other spanish works and periods which I haven't studied. However, the teachers were always very helpful and explained things nicely to me as they knew I was an exchange student, so generally there wasn't any big problems. The level of the courses were perfect for me, of course it did take a bit longer to study as everything was in spanish, but I quickly got used to it and it was actually not a problem at all in the end. Overall I did just as well, and better, than the spanish students so I am very satisfied.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at Complutense was centrered around the professor who would talk most of the time, however there were also discussions and open questions in the classrooms. A big difference I noticed is that the spanish teachers don't give out homework, they just give a list of books which need to be read for the exam. Another difference to the UCPH is that in copenhagen I am used to more group work, however I personally prefer individual work so the style of teaching at UCM fit well for me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cervantes y su tiempo.
Literatura del siglo XVII.
Fundamentos filosóficos para el estudio de la lengua y la literatura.
Retórica y crítica literaria.
Introducción a la cultura y mitología clásica.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the 'Fundamentos Filosóficos para el estudio de la lengua y la literatura' because it was a subject where I as an exchange student could contribute a lot by having a different perspective than the spanish students. I had a great teacher who was very nice to engage in dialogue with me and gave me space to express my thoughts. At the same time it was a subject which combined philosophy with literature in a way that I did not expect and which was super interesting. 

Generally I would recommend all the courses because they were all really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up buying more books than I expected, but that is also part of my hobby and it wasn't strictly necesary for the university.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was a bit expensive, but apart from that thing such as food and transport is really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't get an introduction to the posible clubs/sports at the Complutense, so I actually don't really know what oportunities I had.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some conferences and also some sort of music festival.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN trips are a great oportunity both to meet knew people and to see spain.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are lots of things to see in Madrid and because of it's central location it is easy to travel to different parts of Spain as well. I went to Galicia and Alicante, both really nice cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy for me, as I have lived in Madrid before and know my way around.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's good if you can speak in spanish to them, because many students don't feel very comfortable speaking in english. It's also easy to make friends hanging out in the cafeteria at the university or going to a local taberna after studying.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way of studying was a bit difficult in the beginning because the professors don't give homework for each day so I had to figure out a routine myself.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Living in Malasaña was really lovely and I really enjoyed being able to speak spanish all the time and also visiting the different museums in Madrid.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That it's good to read the texts in the beginning and during the semester, even though the teacher might not mention them in the class until the end, because at the end of the semester all exams and papers are at the same time so there isn't a lot of time to study. It is also quite important to get some spanish friends as they can help you with all the questions you might have. And lastly one must remember to enjoy it and say yes to the experience because it's over really quickly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's always ok to write to the Erasmus office, they're really good at giving information.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic courses I took really enriched my experience as I have learned a lot and gained more knowledge in a field that I now know I want to continue studying. I was also really rewarding to get spanish friends as I have practised my spanish a lot and become really comfortable in the language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Studying for the exams was a bit tough, but I managed it very well in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
